recipes.name: Spicy Bok Choy in Garlic Sauce

steps.text: Trim ends from bok choy and discard. Chop bok choy, keeping white stems and green leaves separate. Rinse, then spin or pat dry.
Stir water, garlic, oyster sauce, soy sauce, brown sugar, ginger, and pepper flakes together in a bowl.

Heat both oils together in a wok over medium-high heat. Add bok choy stems and stir-fry until they start to turn pale green, 2 to 3 minutes. Add bok choy leaves and stir-fry until wilted, 1 to 2 minutes. Remove from the heat and transfer to a serving dish.
Pour sauce into the wok and return to the stovetop over medium-high heat. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce has thickened slightly, about 3 minutes.
Pour sauce over bok choy and toss lightly to coat.

raw_recipe.headline: Spicy Bok Choy in Garlic Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This garlic bok choy is ready in minutes after a quick stir-fry. A sweet, gingery sauce with pepper flakes adds umami goodness to this subtle vegetable.

review.reviewBody:
Thanks to Fishyon for pointing out the error in my recipe. In step 3, I forgot to say what to do with the other half of the oil. Step 3 should read:

Heat half of the oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add the bok choy stems first; stir fry for a few minutes or until the pieces start to turn a pale green. When stems are almost cooked, add the remaining oil and the leaves; cook and stir until leaves are wilted, 1 to 2 minutes. Remove from the heat and transfer the bok choy to a serving dish. Pour the sauce into the skillet or wok, and set over medium-high heat. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce has thickened slightly, about 3 minutes. Pour over the bok choy and toss lightly to coat. 

Once the recipe is published, Allrecipes will not make changes to it. They suggested that I post a comment here which seems odd since I have to include a rating. Naturally, it gets five stars!

Wow, wow, wow! Fantastic! I added 8 oz. sliced mushrooms just after the stems, then added cherry tomatoes to the empty skillet before heating the sauce. Removed the tomatoes after a couple minutes, made the sauce, then threw everything back and tossed. Served it over brown rice for a delicious, meatless meal. I didn't have or want oyster sauce --- just added an extra tsp of soy sauce and used only 2 tsp brown sugar.

This was really tasty! I had way less than a pound of bok choy, but made the full amount of sauce and let everyone sauce their own plate to taste. I used hoisin sauce in place of the oyster and didn't have fresh ginger so sprinkled some ground in the mix. The sauce is really good, so I kept what we didn't use and have been randomly using it as a dip when snacking. I will probably use this sauce in other recipes in the future.

Great flavors! The ginger really makes this dish! I didn't have oyster sauce, so used 1:1 soy sauce:hoisin sauce and this dish came out amazing, so I assume that was a good substitute! :)
I topped with black sesame seeds before serving.

We loved this recipe!!!! We added sliced mushrooms to it and didn't add the brown sugar. Next time (tomorrow) I will add 1 tbs of corn starch to the sauce. Thank you for this recipe. It has so much flavor.
I doubled the sauce, and sautéed 5 boneless, skinless chicken thighs with1 T oyster sauce in oil before reducing the sauce. Delicious!, Kids loved it!

I love this! To make it into a full meal, I add shrimp and serve over rice. Plus I try to brown the bok choy a little and it seems to take on the Sauce faster than not doing so. I've made this twice now. The second time I used a little less water and the sauce thickened up so nicely.

This has become my go to recipe for bok choy. I just love it! FYI, I usually substitute fish sauce for the oyster sauce since I have that on hand, plus I add a wee bit of hoisin sauce and actually cook the garlic with the veggies. Tastes amazing!

reading through the reviews i was worried this was going to be a little boring so i made a few changes.. i was looking for inspiration for a sauce to put over some stir fried veggies.. i left out the veg oil, stir fried the veggies (carrots, celery, squash, orange baby bell peppers & mushrooms) in the sesame oil, subbed fresh squeezed orange juice for the water, used regular soy sauce, subbed honey for the brown sugar (only using half the amount), and added 1/4 tsp of chinese five spice and some cornstarch to thicken up the sauce.. this would go great over rice or quinoa.. ty for the start of a tasty dish
I added the sauce to the pan along with the bok choy instead of letting it thicken separately. It was delicious. I used Shanghai bok choy instead of baby bok choy.

My husband & I enjoyed this dish very much! I did add two ingredients in the recipe: fish tofu, tempe, and Indonesian sweet soy sauce (Ketjap Manis is the brand). I got the fish tofu from local Asian store and Whole Foods market for the other. I would cook tempe first with cooking oil (per recipe) then added the rest per recipe. I would think just add all ingredients per recipe would have been great! I just wanted to use other ingredients before they go bad. Enjoy!
Only changes I made were to use split baby bok choi. I did not seperate leaves and stems, and I added enoki mushrooms. Dish was superb, and loved by all who tasted it.
I’m so glad I made this recipe. I used baby bok choy and it’s so quick to cook. Thank you

As a Chinese person myself, I have to say this is not it. The sauce is super watery and doesn't need water to begin with as the bok choy release water too. The sauce doesn't stick to the bok choy and the end result is pretty bland and unflavorful. I'd go somewhere else for bok choy.

This was so delicious! The only suggestion I have is if you are using full grown bok choy (not baby) you should cook the stems a lot longer, otherwise they will be too crunchy and won’t absorb the sauce much. Cook time will depend on your liking. Otherwise the flavors were wonderful! Thanks so much for sharing!!!
